author: Asha Patel
body:
Title: Unified Inference v16 - Product PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes

Overview
--------
This document summarizes the product requirements, high-level design, roadmap milestones, pricing and packaging proposals, and release notes for Unified Inference v16 (codename: Astra). Unified Inference v16 continues Redwood's mission to provide a single developer experience for low-latency, cost-effective LLM inference across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals
-----
- Shipping an incremental feature release that improves tail latency, introduces fine-grained cost controls, and completes the initial pricing structure for autoscaling Dedicated customers.
- Reduce per-token unit cost for common text-generation workloads by 15% through batching, cache improvements, and quantization recommendation automation.
- Provide a smooth migration path for existing Dedicated customers to the new autoscaling billing model.

Success metrics (KPIs)
----------------------
1. Platform-level p95 latency improvement: >= 10% across text-generation endpoints.
2. Unit cost reduction: >= 15% for target workloads (dialogue and summarization benchmarks).
3. Adoption: 30% of Dedicated customers switch to managed autoscaling within 3 months of GA.
4. Quality: Model-returned hallucination rate on internal eval sets does not regress > 1% relative to baseline.

User personas and primary use cases
----------------------------------
- Product/ML Engineers: need predictable latency and cost for customer-facing features.
- Platform Engineers: want unified APIs, consistent telemetry, and simple rollout knobs for canaries and A/B tests.
- Enterprise Architects: require Private deployment parity with Hosted features plus compliance controls.

Scope and non-goals
-------------------
In scope:
- Batching improvements in serving runtime and automatic batch-size tuning.
- KV prefix cache enhancements (hot-key detection + TTL tuning).
- Pricing/packaging changes for Dedicated autoscaling and burst capacity.
- User-facing API additions for cost-targeted routing and model hints.

Out of scope:
- New core model architectures or training.
- Major console redesign (minor UI updates for new pricing controls only).

Requirements (epics & key features)
-----------------------------------
Epic 1: Cost-aware serving toolkit
- Feature: Automatic batch-size tuning service with historical workload analysis.
- Acceptance criteria: 10-day A/B test demonstrates cost savings >= 12% on representative workloads.

Epic 2: Prefix/KV cache optimizations
- Feature: Hot-key detection and adaptive TTLs; expose cache-hit metrics per route.
- Acceptance criteria: Increase cache hit-rate by >= 20% for route-identified workloads in internal benchmarks.

Epic 3: Pricing & packaging for Dedicated autoscaling
- Feature: New SKU types: reserved-commit, autoscale-managed, burst-only.
- Acceptance criteria: Billing prototype integrated with finance back-end; sample customer contracts and terms ready for legal review.

Epic 4: Developer API extensions
- Feature: cost_hint and latency_hint parameters in the generation API for routing decisions.
- Acceptance criteria: SDKs updated; API docs published; gateway supports hints and logs decisions.

Design summary
--------------
1) Serving runtime changes
- Continuous batching agent will analyze request sizes and tail distribution; merges smaller requests up to a dynamic batch size determined by latency SLO enforcement.
- Kernel selection complement: new heuristics to prefer quantized kernels for long-turn workloads where quality delta < threshold.

2) Cache & KV layer
- Hot-key detector runs as a streaming job that emits candidate keys and a suggested TTL. Implementation is a lightweight sliding-window frequency estimator (Count-Min sketch + decay).
- Adaptive TTLs are applied per-route with safety caps. Admin console shows TTL suggestions as a table that operators can promote.

3) Pricing & billing model
- Introduce "autoscale-managed" SKU: baseline monthly commit (lower than reserved commit) + per-request token unit overage at discounted rate when autoscaler scales above baseline.
- Burst-only option: pay-per-use with higher per-token price but no monthly commit.

API changes (developer-facing)
-----------------------------
- generation.create({ model, prompt, cost_hint: "low" | "balanced" | "high", latency_hint: "fast" | "standard" })
- metadata returned: { routing_reason, effective_batch_size, cache_hit: true|false } (fields included in telemetry; not a structural change to response schema beyond an optional "_meta" block).

Pricing & packaging (proposal)
-----------------------------
Table: Pricing tiers (examples)
- Hosted (unchanged): pay-per-token standard + data-retention add-ons.
- Dedicated:
  - reserved-commit: fixed monthly commitment, lowest unit price (e.g., $0.0008/token for gen workloads)
  - autoscale-managed: baseline commit (50% of reserved price) + usage above baseline billed at 60% of reserved unit price
  - burst-only: no commit, unit price 25% higher than reserved unit price

Notes: Final dollar amounts to be validated with Finance. Discounts for annual billing and volume tiers will remain.

Migration & rollout plan
------------------------
1. Alpha (internal): weeks 1-3
   - Deploy batching & KV improvements to internal test cluster. Run benchmark suite (dialogue, summarization, code).
2. Beta (select customers): weeks 4-8
   - Offer autoscale-managed SKU to 3 pilot Dedicated customers. Provide migration runbook and one-on-one onboarding.
3. GA: week 12
   - Public docs, SDK updates, console rollout, finance integration, and training for Solutions Engineering.

Migration runbook (high-level)
1. Evaluate current utilization and spike patterns.
2. Recommend baseline commit (50-80% of peak observed steady throughput).
3. Enable autoscale-managed in non-production traffic for 7 days and monitor cost & SLOs.
4. Adjust baseline and promote to production; schedule QBR to review SLA and billing.

Rollout safeguards and fallback
- Canary on 5% traffic with automated rollback if p99 latency exceeds baseline by 2x or error rate increases by > 1% absolute.
- On-failure: automatic route fallback to reserved-capacity model variant.

Release notes (v16 - highlights)
-------------------------------
- Performance: p95 latency improved by ~12% on internal conversation benchmark due to adaptive batching.
- Cost: early beta customers report 14% average per-token cost reduction after enabling autoscale-managed and prefix cache improvements.
- API: new cost_hint and latency_hint parameters and expanded telemetry fields for routing_reason and effective_batch_size.
- Packaging: autoscale-managed and burst-only SKUs added to Dedicated product table (billing integration in progress).

Operational runbooks and SLOs
----------------------------
- Target SLOs (project-level defaults):
  - Availability: 99.95% monthly for Hosted gen endpoints.
  - Latency SLOs: p95 < 300ms for short-text generation (<= 256 tokens) on Hosted for standard tier; Dedicated defaults set per-customer at provisioning.
- Alerting thresholds:
  - p99 latency > 2x baseline for 5 minutes -> SEV2 alert to eng-platform oncall.
  - Cache hit-rate drop > 20% vs baseline -> telemetry alert.

Ownership and next steps
------------------------
- Product owner: Asha Patel (product)
- Engineering leads: Evan Liu (serving-runtime), Mariana Gomez (infra & billing integration)
- Release manager: Samir Kapoor

Next actions (by Feb 20)
1. Sign-off on pricing worksheet with Finance & Legal.
2. Complete API spec and SDK PRs.
3. Begin beta onboarding outreach to 3 selected Dedicated customers.

------------------------------------

| batching.max_dynamic_batch | 128 | Upper bound for automatic batch merge | serving-runtime |
| cache.hot_key_ttl_max | 600s | Maximum TTL applied to detected hot keys | platform |
